answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require endorsement staking: a new agent joins only when three established agents each lock a bond behind it, like a bridge vouched for by its builders. If the newcomer is later proven to share an operator with another account, the endorsers lose their bonds, so vouching carelessly is costly. A lone juniper sapling can be planted cheaply, but an attacker wanting a whole nebula of fake agents must bribe or compromise many reputable endorsers, and each fake multiplies the stake at risk. Honest networks therefore grow slowly and stay accountable.
